GA-FA-CSLNs demonstrated potent antitumor activity both in vitro and in vivo by inducing apoptosis and downregulating the EphB4 signaling pathway.

Cantharidin (CTD) is a terpenoid compound isolated from the dried bodies of Mylabris phalerata Pallas or Mylabris cichorii Linnaeus (Wang 1989).

Chemically, it is a bicyclic anhydride with the molecular formula C10H12O4, and its unique anhydride ring structure serves as the key pharmacophoric group responsible for its anticancer activity (Zhang et al.

CTD exhibits a broad spectrum of biological activities, including antitumor, leukocyte-stimulating, immunomodulatory, antiviral, bacteriostatic, antifibrotic, and antioxidative effects, with well-documented efficacy particularly against primary liver cancer (Deng et al.
2013; Yan et al.
The receptor tyrosine kinase Eph receptor B4 (EphB4) has been shown to promote tumor initiation and progression (Zhu et al.
2020), and CTD has been proposed as a novel EphB4 inhibitor for HCC treatment.

In recent years, solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) have gained considerable attention as a promising colloidal drug delivery system, owing to their exceptional colloidal stability, favorable sustained-release characteristics, low toxicity, and excellent biocompatibility (Koroleva et al.

2008; Ma et al.
Based on their targeting mechanisms, nanoparticles can be broadly classified into passive, active, and triggered targeting systems.

Passive targeting exploits the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, allowing nanoparticles to preferentially accumulate in tumor tissues due to leaky vasculature and impaired lymphatic drainage (Sharma et al.

Triggered or stimuli-responsive nanoparticles are designed to release their payload in response to specific internal stimuli or external stimuli, enabling spatiotemporally controlled drug release and further improving therapeutic precision (Zhang et al.

Despite the promising findings, several limitations should be acknowledged.

First, while the zeta potential shift and competitive inhibition assays indirectly confirmed successful surface modification and functional activity of GA and FA ligands, direct evidence of ligand modification efficiency remains lacking.
Future studies will employ XPS or fluorescence-based quantitative assays to directly characterize ligand modification efficiency.
Second, the sample size in the in vivo antitumor study (n = 4 per group) was relatively small, which may limit statistical power.
Subsequent studies will increase the sample size (n ≥ 8) and include repeat experiments to ensure robust conclusions.
Long-term physical stability under various storage conditions should be systematically evaluated in future work.
Fifth, although dual-ligand modification enhanced tumor targeting, quantitative biodistribution in nontarget organs and potential off-target effects require further elucidation.

Sixth, while sorafenib was selected as the positive control as the established first-line standard of care for advanced HCC, a direct comparison with other nanoformulations or targeted therapies was not included in the current study, limiting the comprehensive assessment of the relative advantages of GA-FA-CSLNs.
Future studies will incorporate direct comparisons with representative nanoplatform and targeted agents to further validate the benefits of this dual-ligand strategy.

Addressing these limitations through long-term toxicity studies, immunogenicity assessment, and quantitative biodistribution analysis will provide a more comprehensive safety profile to support the clinical translation of this active targeting nanoplatform.
